name: line-sidebar

frames.best_why: The full twelve-row list is visible, with the active row accented purple and no cursor over it.

tagline: Menu labels slide right and glow purple near the cursor.
summary: A vertical menu where each numbered label and its short tick react to pointer proximity, shifting right and turning purple. Clicking a row sets a lasting accent and grows the marker beside it.
appearance: A narrow column of twelve small numbered labels, each preceded by a thin grey rule, evenly stacked on a black field. The active row is tinted purple and pushed right, and rows near it extend their ticks and brighten.
behaviour: As the pointer moves down the list, rows within reach slide right, shift toward purple and stretch their tick marks like a fisheye. Clicking a row keeps it accented and lengthens the marker line beside it.
demo_content: Twelve docs menu labels from Overview to Support, including Components, Showcase and Changelog.
search_phrases: vertical menu that reacts to cursor
sidebar with shifting text on hover
menu items that slide when hovered
use_when: A docs or app sidebar needs a compact, cursor-aware menu with a clear active page.
avoid_when: The proximity effect is pointer-only, so touch and keyboard users get no feedback from it.
customise: Items, accent, text and marker colours, index and marker visibility, proximity radius, max shift, falloff, marker length and gap, tick scale, item gap, font size and smoothing are props.
weight_why: One rAF loop eases CSS variables on twelve short rows and stops when settled.

a11y.note: Rows are plain list items with click handlers, so Tab never reaches them and there is no focus ring; aria-current marks the active row.

issues: The rows are clickable list items, so keyboard users cannot reach or activate any menu entry.
polish_why: Crisp typography and a restrained fisheye; the feedback is subtle enough to be missed.
